title: InterPruner: Interactive Structured Pruning via Taylor-Implicit Criterion and Language-Prior Modulator for Multimodal Object Detection
summary: Multimodal object detection proves effective in remote sensing, especially the RGB-Infrared paradigm. The parallel feature extractors provide rich multimodal information for robust detection, yet introduce substantial channel redundancy and computational overhead. Existing pruning methods can reduce channel redundancy, but they are designed for unimodal backbones, overlooking cross-modal interactions and dynamic scene-wise redundancy. In this paper, we propose InterPruner, the first interactive structured channel pruning framework for RGB-infrared object detectors. Specifically, we first derive a Taylor-Implicit Criterion(TIC) to quantify channel importance via high-order Taylor expansion and the implicit function theorem. Then, a Modality Interaction Redundancy Analyzer (MIRA) identifies redundant channels via mutual compensability assessment. Finally, a Scene-Prior Channel Anchor (SPCA) uses language priors as semantic anchors to measure channel-scene relevance for dynamic channel importance estimation. Cross-modality channel pruning for RGB-Infrared detection is yet unexplored. Extensive experiments on RGB-infrared object detection dataset demonstrate that InterPruner maintains high performance with negligible degradation. Specifically, it even achieves a 0.6% mAP increase on the FLIR dataset when pruning 50% of the channels. Code will be available on GitHub to facilitate future work.

title: SAR2Agri: Learning SAR Intensity Representations for Agricultural Monitoring
summary: Agricultural monitoring faces unique challenges, arising from the landscape's complex temporal, phenological, and climate dynamics, yet monitoring them is critical for ensuring food security. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites offer all-weather day-night imaging capability supporting key monitoring tasks including crop type mapping, yield prediction and phenological event detection. Existing multimodal remote sensing foundation models including TerraMind and CopernicusFM learn SAR representations by grounding them in optical imagery using joint encoding and contrastive learning techniques, while SAR-specific foundation models such as SAR-JEPA, SARMAE, and SAR-W-MixMAE primarily focus on target detection, flood mapping, and land cover classification applications. Recent work has introduced phenology inspired temporal pretext tasks with optical imagery which has shown strong performance on agricultural downstream tasks. In this work, we propose the first self-supervised learning pipeline focused on using only SAR intensity imagery for agricultural applications. We improve the temporal pretext tasks through masking and curriculum learning to enhance the pretraining pipeline's ability to capture phenological features from SAR. On the SICKLE benchmark, our final model achieves 84.9% IoU on crop type mapping, outperforming optical baselines (by 15.3 pt) and existing SAR baselines (by 2.2 pt), demonstrating the effectiveness of our proposed pipeline for pretraining SAR intensity encoders for agricultural monitoring.
relevance_matches: remote_sensing: remote sensing, synthetic aperture radar

AI.tldr: Proposes the first self-supervised learning pipeline using only SAR intensity imagery for agricultural monitoring, achieving 84.9% IoU on crop type mapping on the SICKLE benchmark.
AI.research_relevance: Moderate relevance. The paper addresses remote sensing (SAR satellite) and mentions "target detection" in related work, but its core task is agricultural monitoring (crop type mapping, phenological event detection), not object detection of vehicles, ships, or aircraft. No lightweighting, compression, or deployment considerations are discussed. The deterministic relevance score of 9 appears to be an overestimate for this research direction.
AI.task_and_scene: Task: Agricultural monitoring including crop type mapping, yield prediction, and phenological event detection. Sensor/modality: SAR intensity imagery (single modality, no optical). Target classes: Crop types (not discrete object instances). Scene: Agricultural landscapes, temporal/phenological dynamics.
AI.model_architecture: Self-supervised learning pipeline with a SAR intensity encoder. Uses temporal pretext tasks enhanced by masking and curriculum learning. The specific backbone architecture (e.g., ViT, CNN) is not specified in the abstract. The model is pretrained on SAR intensity data only, without optical grounding.
AI.lightweight_method: None. The paper does not address model lightweighting, pruning, quantization, distillation, NAS, or any efficiency-oriented design. The focus is entirely on representation learning quality for agricultural tasks.
AI.onboard_deployability: Abstract does not specify any deployment evidence. No parameters, FLOPs, latency, memory, energy, or hardware (edge, FPGA, NPU) information is reported. Onboard or in-orbit inference is not discussed.
AI.datasets_and_metrics: SICKLE benchmark. Metric: IoU (Intersection over Union) for crop type mapping. Abstract does not specify other datasets or metrics for yield prediction or phenological event detection.
AI.experiments: Final model achieves 84.9% IoU on crop type mapping, outperforming optical baselines by 15.3 percentage points and existing SAR baselines by 2.2 percentage points. Ablation details (masking, curriculum learning contributions) are not specified in the abstract.
AI.limitations: Abstract does not specify model size, computational cost, or inference speed. No object detection evaluation (only dense pixel-wise crop mapping). No deployment or efficiency analysis. The method is tailored to agricultural phenological patterns and may not transfer to general object detection tasks.
AI.ideas_for_my_research: 1. The temporal pretext task with masking and curriculum learning could be adapted for self-supervised pretraining of lightweight SAR object detectors on temporal satellite data. 2. The finding that SAR-only pretraining can outperform optical baselines suggests that lightweight SAR models could be viable for onboard inference without relying on optical sensors. 3. The SICKLE benchmark's crop mapping setup could serve as a testbed for evaluating lightweight segmentation models, though this is tangential to object detection.
AI.reading_priority: 2/5 — The paper is relevant to SAR remote sensing but does not address object detection of small/man-made targets, nor does it consider model lightweighting or onboard deployment. Its value is limited to potential inspiration for SAR-specific self-supervised pretraining strategies.
